desc:
Three integer arrays a, b and c are each sorted in non-decreasing order and may contain repeats. Return the sorted array of distinct values that appear in all three arrays.

a = [1, 2, 2, 4, 6, 9]
b = [2, 2, 4, 5, 9]
c = [0, 2, 4, 4, 9, 12]
result = [2, 4, 9]

If no value is shared by all three arrays, return an empty array.
constraints: Each array is sorted in non-decreasing order
hints: Intersecting with sets works, but it ignores the sorted order. Try to extend the two-array merge walk to three arrays.
Keep three pointers. If the three current values are not all equal, which pointers can safely move?

Let m be the largest of the three current values. Any pointer sitting on a value smaller than m can never match, so advance it. If all three are equal, record the value (skip it if it equals the last recorded one) and advance all three.
editorial: Use one pointer per array. Let m = max(a[i], b[j], c[k]). A pointer whose value is below m points at something that cannot be present in the array that holds m at or after its pointer, so it is safe to advance it. When all three values equal m, the value is common to all arrays: record it unless it was just recorded (repeats), then advance all three pointers.

The loop stops as soon as any pointer reaches the end of its array, because nothing more can be common. Every iteration advances at least one pointer, so the work is O(n + m + p) with O(1) extra space beyond the output.
